narrative.overview:
Neutral gray surfaces and a quiet companion give Kith a friendly, low-chrome setting. Open space and readable conversation carry the experience. Ink defines primary actions, links, focus rings, and neutral navigation selection. Blue belongs to the original companion artwork.

The shared web UI also runs inside Electron. The saved assistant name appears in the sidebar, header, and composer, defaulting to Kith; personalization keeps the original companion artwork and existing text hierarchy. Density stays compact in navigation and contextual lists while the conversation has room to breathe. Details appear in contextual panels; the persistent composer and conversation remain the visual anchor. Native setup shares the semantic palette but keeps its own window controls and form geometry.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral surfaces with ink actions and selection.
Compact controls around a spacious conversation.
Contextual detail and restrained, reduced-motion-aware transitions.

rules.name: The Ink Controls Rule
rules.body: Use semantic primary for actions, neutral tones for navigation, and success, warning, or destructive only for meaningful status. Identity color belongs to avatars.

rules.name: The Quiet Labels Rule
rules.body: Use sentence case and modest weight for navigation and section labels. Keep long reading content at regular weight.

rules.name: The Tonal Depth Rule
rules.body: Use surface tone, fine borders, and spacing to separate persistent regions. Reserve soft shadows for floating controls and overlays.

dos: Do consume the shared semantic CSS variables and generate palette CSS from the TypeScript source.
Do reuse the shared Base UI primitives before adding custom controls.
Do keep state legible through text and accessible names as well as color.
Do preserve the conversation and composer when opening contextual details.
Do respect system appearance, keyboard focus, and reduced motion.
Do use the original companion asset with empty alternative text when adjacent text names the assistant.
donts: Don't recolor ordinary controls with the companion's blue identity.
Don't turn secondary details into permanent explanatory chrome.
Don't replace semantic colors with fixed light-theme or dark-theme colors.
Don't reproduce proprietary reference artwork or branding.
Don't carry forward legacy glyph icons, uppercase eyebrow treatments, or fixed-white labels as new system patterns.
